32.0.0.en: 1- "Blessed is he whose iniquity is forgiven, and whose sin is covered."

32.0.1.en: 1- David shows his joy at the forgiveness of his sins after he had committed his abominable sin, which was adultery and murder, so he says, happy is the one whose sins God forgives, so that He lifts them and removes them from him, and casts them into the sea of forgetfulness.

32.0.2.en: 2- God in His love covers the sins of the penitent, so they do not appear again, that is, He blots them out. And this is a divine love that surpasses the mind, because the thing that troubles man most is his sin. And God in His love removes it completely.

32.0.3.en: 3- If the first psalm speaks to us of the happiness of the one who walks uprightly and keeps away from evil, this one speaks to us of the man who is exposed to falling during his life on earth, but who loves God and His commandments, so he returns to God in repentance, and then receives His forgiveness, and rejoices in this forgiveness.

32.0.4.en: 4- From this verse we understand that forgiveness is a free divine gift that God gives to the penitent; God has compassion on His weak children if they sin and return to Him in repentance, and He blots out their sins from them as if they had not done them.

32.1.0.en: 2- "Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth no sin, and in whose spirit there is no guile."

32.1.1.en: 1- Happy and joyful is the one whose sins God forgives, and who consequently becomes pure, and in this purity stands before God and beholds Him, and no sin appears in him before all the heavenly beings, so it becomes his right to enjoy God while he is on earth, until he reaches Him in heaven.

32.1.2.en: 2- As this man enjoys God's forgiveness and the purity of his heart, he feels the guilt of sin and the sweetness of purity, so he keeps away from all evil and all guile, that is, he is careful in his life and his spirit becomes pure, not wanting to sin because of its preoccupation with God.

32.1.3.en: 3- Sin defiles man, and this defilement is first of the spirit, then of the body, because out of the abundance of the heart the tongue speaks. But harder still is for guile to exist in man's spirit, for he deceives himself, and not God of course. And this guile makes him persist in sin, so it dwells inside him and appears on his body, such as his speech, his glances and his actions; therefore whoever is purified from guile becomes truly pure.

32.1.4.en: 4- St. Paul the Apostle quoted (vv. 1, 2) from this psalm and said them in (Rom 4:6-8), confirming the importance of the work of God's grace in the forgiveness of man's sins, and not the works of the Law.

32.2.0.en: 3- "When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long."

32.2.1.en: 1- After David fell he kept silent and did not confess his sin before God, nor before the priest, nor did he offer a sacrifice for his sin, nor before a prophet like Nathan; therefore his conscience pricked him, and he tried to flee from it, so he remained troubled, having lost his peace.

32.2.2.en: 2- The reproach of David's conscience to him did not quiet down, especially since David is a spiritual man who knows God and His commandments well, and the reproach of conscience wearied David, not only in his spirit, which was troubled, but his body was also affected. And David expresses the depth of his pains and says "my bones waxed old," that is, he suffered many inner troubles until his bones, which are the strongest thing inside the body, almost wasted away and dissolved.

32.2.3.en: 3- David's distress and his being affected by the reproach of his conscience appeared in the sighing of his aching heart every day and all day long, and he expressed this in that he was in pain with every breath that came out of his nose, that is, he was in constant pain, and perhaps this sighing was with a loud cry, either within himself or even in a loud audible voice, which those around him did not understand, or perhaps they thought he was suffering from something; so that some of them said that he was struck with a bodily illness from the great reproach of his conscience to him.

32.2.4.en: 4- David's silence is silence from prayer and praising God, for sin keeps God away from us and separates us from Him, so we lose our enjoyment of Him, and our prayers weaken or stop, but by repentance the ability to pray can be regained.

32.3.0.en: 4- "For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer. Selah."

32.3.3.en: 1- The hand of God was a support to David, but when he sinned the hand of God became heavy upon him until he repented; for after he sinned with the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and a child was born of the adultery, David prayed, but the child died, then Amnon the son of David sinned with his sister Tamar, and after that his brother Absalom killed him, then fled, and after his return he stirred up the people and removed David from his throne and drove him out of the kingdom. All this is the hand of God that became heavy upon David, that his repentance might deepen and he receive the mercies of God.

32.3.4.en: 2- Because of the tribulations that God allowed to come upon David, his inner life turned from moisture, that is, the enjoyment of God's work in him, to severe dryness, so he felt distress and pressure, and then he took refuge in God, who forgave him and removed his sin from him.

32.3.5.en: 3- This verse ends with the word Selah, which is a musical note, and means here the asking of God's mercies, because David is in distress and needs God's compassion and tenderness.

32.4.0.en: 5- "I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah."

32.4.1.en: 1- David arrived at the solution of his problem, which is confessing his sin before God, and before his man Nathan the prophet, and in this he was rid of his sin, since God removed it and lifted it from him.

32.4.2.en: 2- David overcame the barrier of shame and pride by confessing his sin and not hiding it, and his confession was a public confession, so that he even wrote it in his psalms, and he abased himself before God, since he felt the guilt of his sin, and his honor before people no longer mattered to him.

32.4.3.en: 3- The confession that David made declares his rejection and hatred of sin, and the exposing of Satan who made him fall, and in this David regained his sonship to God, who forgave him and restored his purity to him.

32.4.4.en: 4- God's lifting David's sin from him gave David inner peace, but God allowed him a punishment in the problems that he went through, which we mentioned in the previous verse. For although God had forgiven his sin, by this discipline He wanted to deepen the thought of repentance within David, so that afterward he would reject any sin.

32.4.5.en: 5- God in His love wants to forgive the sins of His children, but He waits for their repentance and confession, and then He hastens to forgive, and restores them to their sonship to Him, so they enjoy His care. This is because when Nathan confronted David he confessed his sin at once, unlike what happened with Cain, whom God warned to confess the sin of killing his brother, and he answered insolently and said, "Am I my brother's keeper?" and so he was not forgiven (Gen 4:9). David and Cain both fell into sin, but David confessed with humility before God, while Cain answered God with shamelessness and pride.

32.4.6.en: 6- This verse ends with the word Selah, which is a musical note, and means here thanking God and rejoicing in His forgiveness. In this it differs from the word Selah that is in the previous verse, for the two notes are different according to the meaning of the verse preceding the word Selah.

32.5.0.en: 6- "For this shall every one that is godly pray unto thee in a time when thou mayest be found: surely in the flood of great waters it shall not come nigh unto him."

32.5.1.en: 1- Because God is the forgiver of sins, every person who fears God and lives with Him believes in His love and hastens to Him with repentance to receive His forgiveness.

32.5.2.en: 2- Prayer is not only for confessing sin and obtaining forgiveness, but whoever is godly and falls into sin feels that it keeps God away from him and weakens his prayer, so he hastens to repentance and regains his prayer, and it even becomes warmer because of his feeling of his need for God.

32.5.3.en: 3- When the godly person feels repentance for his sin, at this time he can find the merciful God, to whom he prays confessing his sins, and so receives His forgiveness.

32.5.4.en: 4- Whoever is always godly and fears God feels His constant presence, for God is present at all times, and therefore prayer is available to man at all times.

32.5.5.en: 5- When severe tribulations pass over a person, until he almost perishes as happened in the days of the flood, he hastens to God with repentance, and no harm comes to him; rather, God rescues him, as He rescued Noah and his family.

32.5.6.en: 6- The flood of great waters signifies the day of judgment, when the wicked ask the mountains and hills to cover them, but the children of God suffer no harm; rather, when God appears He takes them to Himself and satisfies them with His love.

32.5.7.en: The door of repentance and confession is the greatest grace that God gives us, so hasten to Him with repentance if you fall into sin, confident of His love and forgiveness, and in proportion to your sense of the guilt of sin offer prayers and tears before God throughout your life, and so your tears mingle with feelings of peace, joy and thanksgiving to God who forgave your sin.

32.6.s.en: (2) Blessings for those who trust in Him

32.6.0.en: 7- "Thou art a covering for me; thou shalt preserve me from trouble; thou shalt compass me about with songs of deliverance. Selah."

32.6.1.en: Compass me about: surround me on every side.

32.6.2.en: 1- When God sees the repentance of His children He covers them, so they are not exposed before people; for if they expose Satan by repentance He covers them, but if they hide their sins they are exposed before people, especially on the last day.

32.6.3.en: 2- God's covering of the penitent also means that He protects him from falling into new sins, whether the same sin into which he fell, or any other sins.

32.6.4.en: 3- If tribulations pass over this penitent for his discipline, God keeps him in them, so that he does not fall into sin, but learns from the discipline and returns to God with all his heart, that is, lives a deeper repentance.

32.6.5.en: 4- When God delivers the penitent from many sins, he rejoices and praises God and sings to Him, and so he enjoys prayer. And thus his heart is filled with joy, and joy also surrounds him, so it shows on his face as a smile and heart's peace.

32.6.6.en: 5- The word Selah here is a musical note that means joy, praise and thanksgiving.

32.7.0.en: 8- "I will instruct thee and teach thee in the way which thou shalt go: I will counsel thee, mine eye being upon thee."

32.7.1.en: 1- God promises David and all the penitent that He will teach him the way of life with Him, that he may walk in the new life, after being rid of his sin. And this walk of his gives him the enjoyment of fellowship with God, so he rejects sin, and in this He protects him from falling into many sins.

32.7.2.en: 2- The second promise is that God will guide the penitent in the way in which they walk, so that the world cannot deceive them with its crooked ways, however great the world's doubts. And they also overcome all despair and discouragement which block the ways before them, and God guides them to the open way that leads to eternal life.

32.7.3.en: 3- The third promise is that God will counsel him, that he may guard against falling again, and also that he may strive in the way of virtue, so that his fellowship with God increases.

32.7.4.en: 4- The fourth promise is God's constant providence and care for him, so that His eye is on the penitent, to keep him from all evil and warn him of any satanic deceit, and to care for him in all his steps, and in this he is established in the way of righteousness.

32.8.0.en: 9- "Be ye not as the horse, or as the mule, which have no understanding: with bit and bridle, whose adornment muzzles them, lest they come near unto thee." Bit: an iron piece placed in the mouth of the horse or the mule to prevent it from walking or running. Bridle: a strip of leather that ties the bit on both sides to control the movement of the horse or the mule. Muzzles: the bit is considered a muzzle, that is, a restraint placed on the mouth of the horse to control its movement.

32.8.1.en: 1- God warns His children not to behave like animals, such as the horse and the mule, which are distinguished by pride and lust, but to be calm and humble, living in purity, that they may enjoy fellowship with God.

32.8.2.en: 2- The bit and bridle are placed in the mouths of the horse and the mule to control them and prevent them from rushing, but in man God has placed the conscience to control him and prevent him from all evil. And in the New Testament He gave him the Holy Spirit, to prick his heart if he sins and to warn him of all evil.

32.8.3.en: 3- The horse and the mule signify the proud, lustful wicked, and God restrains them, so that they do not approach His children and harm them; so He allows tribulations for the wicked, that they may not carry out their evils against the children of God, or He warns them with His commandments and frightens them with the last judgment, that they may keep away from evil.

32.9.0.en: 10- "Many sorrows shall be to the wicked: but he that trusteth in the Lord, mercy shall compass him about."

32.9.2.en: 1- The wicked are exposed to many tribulations, whether external tribulations, such as diseases, problems and external calamities, or inner tribulations, which are the reproach of their consciences to them, for they are always without peace, even if they laugh and indulge in various lusts.

32.9.3.en: 2- The person who lives with God and trusts in Him and repents of his sins receives God's mercies, and in proportion to his repentance God surrounds him with many mercies and blessings, so his trust in God and his enjoyment of His love increase. And God protects him from the snares of the demons, so that he does not fall into the various sins.

32.10.0.en: 11- "Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous: and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart."

32.10.1.en: 1- David concludes the psalm with a call to the children of God to rejoice in God, who protects His children and forgives their sins, and pours out many blessings on them, so that they thank Him and enjoy His blessings.

32.10.2.en: 2- The one who enjoys joy is the one who has acquired a pure, upright heart, then the pure intentions of his heart appear in good conduct, which is the conduct of the righteous; for outward righteousness comes from inner purity, and therefore the joy of the righteous is inward and is not taken away from them, because it is inside their hearts, while the joys of the wicked are outward and passing.

32.10.3.en: 3- If joy is the portion of the righteous, this is divine justice, because the portion of the wicked is sorrows, as in the previous verse; so none can enjoy inner peace and true joy but the children of God, who fear Him.

32.10.4.en: 4- This psalm begins by pronouncing blessed the one whose sins are forgiven, and ends with the joy of the righteous and the upright in heart. This shows the importance of repentance, which lifts man's sins and fills his heart with joy, so that he thanks God at all times.

32.10.5.en: If repentance gives all these blessings, would that we hasten to it every day, indeed immediately after falling, so that we humble ourselves before God, and He pours out on us His mercies and blessings.

32.10.6.en: The shout of victory "Shout for joy in the Lord, O ye righteous) "... v. 1) Introduction:

32.10.7.en: 1- Its author: there is no title for this psalm in the Hebrew text; therefore it is among the orphan psalms, but the Septuagint attributes it to David.

32.10.8.en: 2- When was it said: after David's victory in a battle with the Philistines, in which he was exposed to death at the hand of one of the Philistine champions called "Ishbibenob," but God rescued him with the help of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the son of David's sister (2 Sam 21:16, 17).

32.10.9.en: 3- A liturgical psalm: this psalm was sung in the temple, especially at the feasts, and the choirs would repeat this psalm in response to one another, each choir repeating a verse or several verses, then at the end they would conclude with verses repeated by all together; and these are the last verses in this psalm.

32.10.10.en: 4- A psalm of thanksgiving: this psalm is one of the five psalms of thanksgiving, which are Psalms 30-34. And the beginning of this psalm is connected with the end of the psalm before it.

32.10.11.en: 5- A teaching psalm: because it teaches that God is the strongest power in the world, and the victor over the nations; therefore His people glorify Him.

32.10.12.en: 6- This psalm is not among the psalms of the Agpeya.
